title: Exact invoice totals by customer and currency
prompt: Build a CLI reading a JSON array of invoice rows from stdin. A valid row is an object with customer (nonempty string), currency (three uppercase ASCII letters) and amount (a string of an optional minus sign, digits, and an optional fractional part of one or more digits; no exponent, no spaces). Anything else is an invalid row, identified by its 0-based index. Never use binary floating point. Each valid amount is first rounded to the minor unit of its currency, 0 decimals for JPY and 2 decimals for every other currency, using round-half-to-even on the exact decimal value; then rows are summed exactly per (customer, currency). Never combine different currencies. Print exactly one JSON object and a newline: {groups,rejected}. groups lists one entry per (customer, currency) with at least one valid row, as {customer,currency,total,rows}, where total is a string with exactly the currency's number of decimals (for example "12.50" or "-3.00", or "7" for JPY), never "-0" or "-0.00" (a zero total is written without a minus sign), and rows counts the valid rows; groups are sorted by customer then currency in plain code-unit string order. rejected lists the indices of invalid rows ascending. An empty array gives {"groups":[],"rejected":[]}. Invalid JSON or a non-array root: exit nonzero, leave stdout empty and write a diagnostic to stderr. Exit 0 on success. No external services are needed.
